key_insight: A two-stage neural framework learns dynamical constraints from observations, then searches for admissible extreme structures, with geometry transfer enabled by suitable system symmetries.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support risk analysis, nonlinear forecasting, and anomaly detection by identifying rare, high-impact scenarios beyond observed data.
method: Infer effective dynamical constraints from observational data without assuming governing equations.
Use a geometry-agnostic neural representation when suitable symmetries permit.
Apply physics-informed neural search to discover extreme coherent structures.
evidence_signal: Demonstrations recover a Duffing homoclinic pulse, standing and Townes solitons, and a Liouville instanton through transfer from Lorentzian to Euclidean geometry.
watch_item: Geometry transfer depends on suitable symmetries, and the abstract does not quantify robustness to noisy or limited observations.
paper_title: Geometry-Agnostic Data-Driven Discovery of Extreme Scenarios
